newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds firm, BB-rated paper in demand.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds firm, BB-rated paper in demand.

text.p: U.S. corporate debt prices held firm into the market's close Wednesday despite a weakening in the Treasury market, traders said.
Demand grew for safer, double-B-rated paper following several recent high-profile blowups among junk issuers, they reported.
"A lot of people lost money on Marvel Holdings and MobileMedia bonds. People are questioning the safety of their single-B holdings and moving up to double-Bs," trader said.
The double-B sector has tightened from 10-20 basis points over the past month, traders said.
The deal was several times oversubscribed and saw strong demand from both junk and cross-over investors, market sources said.
In the investment grade-market, prices generally followed Treasuries on moderate trading volume, traders said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury was down 13/32 on Wedesday, ending the day at 101-12/32 to yield 6.40 percent.
Delta Air Lines bonds widened to 135 basis points from 127 basis points over Treasuries on news that the company was in talks to aquire Continental Airlines Inc.
S&P revised Delta's ratings outlook to "developing" from positive on Wednesday, in light of the possible acquisition.

The rating agency stated, "...acquisition of Continental would add approximately $5 billlion of debt and leases to Delta's balance sheet, with possible futher debt to finance the acquistion (which would likely cost over $2 billion)."
S&P added airline mergers have historically caused difficult problems of labor and operation intergration.
It noted however, that some features of Continental's route structure, namely its Houston hub, could strengthen Delta's overall market position.
